inputs.text: The organizers are pushing 8 million across more than 3,300 events in all 50 states, and officials’ silence is convenient: nobody has to verify the number while the headline does the political work. The “about one million” and 600-event increase from October may be less a measure of public sentiment than a way to manufacture inevitability. Whether the figure is inflated or simply left unchallenged, the people shaping the story benefit from making a disputed estimate look like proof of a nationwide uprising. The real contest is over who gets to define public opinion.
